newsitem.title: USA: Enova expects more variability in earnings.
newsitem.headline: Enova expects more variability in earnings.

text.p: Enova Corp, parent of San Diego Gas & Electric Co, expects to see more seasonal variability in quarterly earnings as the result of electricity deregulation in California, the company said Tuesday.
"From now on, earnings will be generally higher during the summer months when we sell more energy and lower in the other months," said David Kuzma, Enova's chief financial officer.
In addition, seasonal fluctuations in fuel costs were expected to affect quarterly earnings.

"Prior to 1997, the regulatory accounting process smoothed out these fluctuations. By the end of the year, these fluctuations are expected to balance out, even though the quarterly variations could be significant," Kuzma said.
Enova reported first-quarter earnings of 42 cents per share, down from 57 cents a year earlier.

If earnings were still calculated as they were in the past, the first-quarter earnings per share for 1997 would have been 65 cents, an eight-cent improvement over the first quarter 1996, the company said.
Enova attributed four cents of the increase to a non-recurring income-tax benefit from the 1995 sale of a former subsidiary, with the remaining 4 cents coming mainly from lower maintenance costs.
California will begin next January to allow open competition between electricity suppliers, phasing-out over as long as four years the current system of regulated monopoly utilities.
Last October, Enova announced plans to merge with Pacific Enterprises, parent of neighboring Southern California Gas Co.
The merger is still undergoing regulatory review.
